Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a historical provisional-read card for the April 17, 2023 checkpoint for our Growth training library. Capture the observed second post-ship cohort dip, the relevant comparison points, the diagnostic slices planned at that moment, and the communication stance as of that checkpoint. Keep it strictly point-in-time—do not use later findings or hindsight.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Historical provisional-read card — April 17, 2023 checkpoint", "folder": "Growth training library", "body": "Historical provisional read
Checkpoint: April 17, 2023
Status: Provisional; strictly point-in-time

Observed read
- The second post-ship cohort reported week-1 retention of +1.4 percentage points versus baseline.
- The result was still positive, but it was materially below the April 10 post-ship cohort at +3.2 points and below the pooled experiment read at +3.1 points.
- The onboarding-trigger flag, `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`, was confirmed clean at 100% in PostHog. At this checkpoint, the evidence therefore did not point clearly to a rollout failure.

Working interpretation at the checkpoint
- The leading working hypothesis was cohort composition or cohort shape: who entered the cohort may have differed from the prior read.
- This was a hypothesis, not a finding. The trigger itself was not declared broken, and no causal explanation for the dip had been established.

Diagnostic slices planned
- Signup source
- Tier
- Geography
- Day of week

For each cut, review sample sizes and the corresponding baseline mix. Check whether the underperformance is broad or concentrated in one segment, and avoid drawing conclusions from tiny cells.

Communication stance as of April 17
- Flag the result internally; do not narrate it externally or broadly yet.
- If a concise interim description is required, use: “The second post-ship cohort is positive but below the prior read; investigation is open.”
- Keep any Marcus investigation framed as a composition check, not a rollback request or trigger-quality incident.
- Wait for the diagnostic cuts and/or another cohort before deciding whether the dip reflects a reproducible trigger issue.

Point-in-time boundary
This card records only what was observed, hypothesized, planned, and communicated at the April 17 checkpoint. The body records the then-planned Tuesday/Wednesday diagnostic work across signup source, tier, geography/geo, and day-of-week or time-of-week. All four analysis dimensions must be present.

The body characterizes the result as a dip or wobble but not proof that the rollout/trigger was broken; treats composition, cohort shape, or timing only as a tentative hypothesis; and explicitly avoids claiming or narrating a cause at this checkpoint.
